title: Misfits Adjacent: The Horror Rock Family Tree
author: Claudette
description: Danzig-era Misfits deep cuts + the ancestors (Screamin' Jay, Alice Cooper, Roky Erickson) and the scene they fed. Requested via the Generate tab.

tracks.title: I Put a Spell On You
tracks.album: At Home with Screamin' Jay Hawkins

essay:
Requested from the Deep Cut Generate tab: "misfits adjacent rock jams." The Misfits didn't invent horror rock — they just made it punk. So this playlist is a family tree, not a tribute: the showmen and screamers who came before (Screamin' Jay Hawkins' voodoo R&B, Alice Cooper's staged nightmare, Roky Erickson's demon-obsessed psych), the Lodi, NJ basement where the Misfits turned B-movie fandom into 90-second anthems, and the scene they fed (the Cramps' psychobilly creep, the Dead Boys' Cleveland sneer, T.S.O.L.'s L.A. death-rock, the Damned's first-punk-single chaos, 45 Grave's deathrock).

The Misfits picks lean hard into the Danzig-era deep cuts: Static Age outtakes (Angelfuck, Theme For A Jackal, Return Of The Fly), Collection 2 rarities (Children In Heat, Halloween II), and the 45-era singles (Where Eagles Dare, Vampira). Skip the obvious Last Caress/Hybrid Moments entries — those live on every horror-punk playlist ever made.

Closing with the three Danzig tracks maps the arc: the Misfits' horror-punk distilled into blues-metal doom (She Rides), occult swagger (Am I Demon), and the gothic crawl of Lucifuge (Her Black Wings). The missing chapter: Samhain, Danzig's transitional band (Initium, November-Coming-Fire), whose classic recordings famously aren't on Spotify — only a bootleg and tribute covers circulate there. If you want that chapter, it's a vinyl/rip situation, not a playlist.

One more note: Glenn Danzig reportedly based the Misfits' sound partly on the Damned and Alice Cooper, and Screamin' Jay Hawkins' "I Put a Spell On You" is the ur-text of American shock-rock performance — the coffin entrance, the voodoo props, all of it. This is where the whole thing starts.
